skill.name: clinvar-database
skill.description: Query ClinVar for human variant clinical significance, review status, E-utilities access, bulk downloads, and VCF annotation guidance.
skill.summary: Search, interpret, and process ClinVar variant evidence for research and genomic medicine workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives from Markdown code spans, public NCBI HTTPS URLs, and benign ClinVar examples. Confirmed issues are limited to unencrypted FTP download guidance and one curl-to-shell installer command that could expose users to tampered remote content.

remediation.issue: FTP URLs are used for ClinVar downloads and installer retrieval.
remediation.suggestion: Replace FTP examples with HTTPS equivalents where available, and tell users to verify checksums for bulk data files.

remediation.issue: The Entrez Direct install example pipes a remotely fetched script directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Change the guidance to download the installer, inspect it, verify its source, and then run it explicitly.

remediation.issue: Shell examples omit integrity checks for downloaded reference data.
remediation.suggestion: Add checksum or signature verification steps before users process downloaded ClinVar archives.

content.value_statement: ClinVar evidence can be hard to search, interpret, and download consistently. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through ClinVar queries, classifications, and data workflows.
actual_capabilities: Build ClinVar search queries by gene, variant, condition, clinical significance, and chromosome.
Explain pathogenic, likely pathogenic, VUS, likely benign, and benign classifications.
Interpret ClinVar review status and star ratings for confidence assessment.
Guide E-utilities API usage for esearch, esummary, efetch, and elink workflows.
Describe bulk ClinVar XML, VCF, and tab-delimited data formats and when to use each.
Support VCF annotation and filtering workflows with ClinVar clinical significance fields.
limitations: It does not replace clinical judgment or a certified genetics professional.
It depends on ClinVar data quality, review status, and release timing.
It cannot guarantee that variant classifications are current without live database checks.
Large bulk data workflows may require local bioinformatics tools and storage.

use_cases.title: Prioritize variants in a research gene list
use_cases.description: Find pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and sort them by ClinVar review status.

use_cases.title: Annotate sequencing results with ClinVar evidence
use_cases.description: Choose the correct ClinVar VCF file and plan a workflow to add clinical significance fields.

use_cases.title: Understand a reported variant classification
use_cases.description: Review what a ClinVar classification means and identify when conflicts or low review status require caution.

prompt_templates.title: Search by gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me search ClinVar for pathogenic variants in BRCA1. Explain the query terms and what review status means.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret a variant record
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the ClinVar meaning of this variant classification: likely pathogenic with two-star review status and no conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a VCF annotation workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a GRCh38 VCF and want to annotate it with ClinVar clinical significance. Outline the safest workflow and key checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a reproducible ClinVar data pull
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible monthly ClinVar bulk download and parsing workflow for a local research database. Include version tracking and validation checks.

output_examples.output: Use a ClinVar query for CFTR, pathogenic clinical significance, and expert panel or practice guideline review status. Review each result for conflicts and access date.

output_examples.input: Should I treat a VUS as diagnostic?
output_examples.output: No. A variant of uncertain significance lacks enough evidence for clinical classification. Escalate to a genetics professional and monitor for reclassification.

output_examples.input: Which ClinVar format should I use for pipeline annotation?
output_examples.output: Use the VCF file that matches your genome build. Use XML only when you need detailed submissions, evidence, and condition relationships.

best_practices: Record the ClinVar release date, genome build, and access date for every analysis.
Prefer expert panel or practice guideline records when prioritizing evidence.
Verify downloaded bulk files before using them in downstream analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not use VUS classifications as diagnostic conclusions.
Do not mix GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates in the same annotation workflow.
Do not ignore conflicting interpretations or low review status.

faq.question: Can this skill diagnose a patient?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret ClinVar data, but clinical decisions require qualified genetics professionals.

faq.question: Which ClinVar file format should I use?
faq.answer: Use VCF for pipeline annotation, XML for complete evidence, and tab-delimited files for quick summaries.

faq.question: What does VUS mean?
faq.answer: VUS means variant of uncertain significance. Current evidence is insufficient to classify it as benign or pathogenic.

faq.question: Why does review status matter?
faq.answer: Review status shows the level of evidence review. Expert panel and practice guideline records usually carry more confidence.

faq.question: Can it use the ClinVar API?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents E-utilities searches, summaries, full record retrieval, and related PubMed links.

faq.question: Does it handle bulk downloads?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains bulk XML, VCF, and tab-delimited downloads, but users should verify file integrity.
